UnitStatement: Deliverable DEL-07-05 is the Results viewer under package PKG-07 (Graphical User Interface and Engineering Workflow).
DEL-07-05 deliverable type is UX_UI_SLICE, scope item SOW-023, objectives OBJ-006 and OBJ-007, context envelope L.
Intended GUI surface is a results viewer for tabular and graphical review.
Result categories in scope are displacements, rotations, forces, moments, restraint reactions, equipment loads, stresses, and ratios.
Architectural route: the GUI reads schema-first command/query/job result envelopes through application services.
Result values must remain unit-aware and dimensionally checked (invariant OPS-K-UNIT-1).
Missing data, assumptions, provenance, nonlinear/convergence issues, and IP boundary warnings must remain visible.
Ratios are displayed only when a user-supplied rule pack and required inputs support the check; incomplete rule input remains an explicit finding.
Viewer content should remain reproducible and handoff-ready for reports and structured result exports.
No protected standards text, protected tables, copied formulas, proprietary thresholds, or certification claims are introduced.
This setup produces GUI planning documents, not GUI source code (FACT).
Exact UI component library, state library, and visual layout details are TBD.
Exact result-envelope schema fields for each displayed category are TBD, owned by schema/result-envelope implementation deliverables.
Exact stress-ratio formulas, thresholds, allowables, or code categories are out of scope for public defaults and are user/rule-pack supplied.
Professional acceptance or code compliance status is out of software authority; human review remains required.
The results viewer should be framed as a review surface over already-produced mechanical, diagnostic, stress, reaction, equipment-load, and user-rule-check result envelopes.

The viewer should not compute solver mechanics, recover stresses, evaluate rule packs, define protected code criteria, or export final reports directly unless a later sealed implementation brief expands scope.
Boundary: mechanics solved is distinct from rule-pack checked.
Boundary: rule-pack pass/fail is distinct from professional approval.
Boundary: missing solve-required or rule-check-required data is a displayed finding.
Boundary: every numerical value remains unit-aware.
Boundary: result displays carry warnings, assumptions, and provenance hooks.
Boundary: public examples and templates use no protected standards data or proprietary engineering values.
The results viewer should make analysis outputs reviewable without hiding the conditions that make those outputs trustworthy, incomplete, or unsuitable for professional reliance.

The viewer helps users inspect mechanics results, user-rule-check outputs, warnings, assumptions, and report/export readiness; it is not a solver, code interpreter, or professional approval mechanism.
Keep result categories visible and separable: displacements, rotations, forces, moments, reactions, equipment loads, stresses, and ratios are related but not interchangeable.
Treat result envelopes and diagnostics as the boundary of authority for what the GUI may show.
Preserve unit and dimensional context at every numerical display.
Show missing solve-required data and rule-check-required data as findings, not as empty success states.
Treat stress ratios as user-rule-pack outputs; do not invent thresholds, allowables, categories, or pass/fail meanings.
Preserve export/report traceability: visible result review should align with reproducibility metadata instead of becoming an isolated screen state.
Keep professional-boundary notices close to result status so software output is not mistaken for certification, sealing, approval, or code compliance.
The result surface is broad enough to require filtering, grouping, and cross-highlighting in a future implementation brief, but this setup does not choose the exact interaction design.
Future implementation should decide result category navigation without changing this document's boundaries.
Future implementation should decide load case and combination selection.
Future implementation should decide envelope/range selection.
Future implementation should decide node, element, support, and equipment-load targeting.
Future implementation should decide tabular values versus graphical overlays.
Future implementation should decide unit display and conversion controls.
Future implementation should decide diagnostic badges, warning panels, and blocked states.
Future implementation should decide report/export readiness indicators.
Trade-off: tables support exact inspection and overlays support spatial pattern recognition; use each where it supports review, and both must remain unit-aware and diagnostics-qualified.
Trade-off: ratios may show user-rule-pack calculations when inputs are complete, but the UI must not turn those ratios into automatic professional approval or public code compliance claims.
Trade-off: filters should not suppress blocking diagnostics or professional-boundary status without a deliberate, visible review state.
Trade-off: the viewer may expose report/export readiness signals, but report generation and structured result exports remain PKG-08 surfaces unless a later sealed brief says otherwise.
Example: a load-combination selection reveals displacements and rotations at selected nodes, with unit labels and any solver diagnostics attached.
Example: a support selection reveals restraint reactions and active-state warnings when nonlinear support state is uncertain.
Example: a stress result view shows mechanical stress values when available and shows RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE if a requested ratio depends on missing user rule-pack inputs.
Example: a report/export readiness indicator shows whether result hashes, solver version, rule-pack checksum, warnings, and assumptions are available for downstream reporting.
No source conflict was identified during setup.

Open issue (TBD): exact UI layout, component library, state library, and overlay behavior.
Open issue (TBD): exact rule-ratio terminology when private rule packs differ by user design basis.

This deliverable specifies the setup basis for a GUI results viewer presenting reviewable analysis outputs for displacements, rotations, forces, moments, restraint reactions, equipment loads, stresses, and user-rule ratios; it is a UX/UI slice under PKG-07 supporting OBJ-006 and OBJ-007.
This setup does not implement GUI source code, tests, schemas, exporter code, solver logic, stress recovery, rule-pack evaluation, report generation, or protected engineering data.
REQ-07-05-001: the viewer shall present result categories listed in SOW-023 when those categories are present in validated result envelopes.

REQ-07-05-002: the viewer shall preserve the architecture boundary; GUI-facing code consumes application-service result envelopes and shall not bypass domain-core unit checks, provenance checks, diagnostics, or public/private data boundaries.

REQ-07-05-003: displayed numerical result values shall be unit-aware and dimensionally labeled; missing or incompatible units shall be shown as diagnostics rather than silently converted or defaulted.

REQ-07-05-004: the viewer shall distinguish mechanics result status, rule-input incompleteness, user-rule-check status, failed user-rule status, and human-review-required status; it shall not expose automatic CODE_COMPLIANT status.

REQ-07-05-005: rule-pack ratios shall be displayed only when required user-supplied rule-pack inputs and checksum/provenance status support the calculation; otherwise the ratio surface shall show an unavailable or blocked state with a diagnostic.

REQ-07-05-006: result review shall keep warnings, assumptions, missing data, solver diagnostics, nonlinear/convergence state, provenance gaps, and IP-boundary warnings visible with the result context they qualify.

REQ-07-05-007: result displays intended for reports or exports shall retain traceability to model version/hash, solver version, rule-pack name/version/checksum, units, warnings, assumptions, and limitations when those envelope fields exist.

REQ-07-05-008: public setup artifacts shall not introduce protected standards text, protected tables, proprietary formulas, code-specific allowables, stress limits, SIF/flexibility values, load-combination defaults, or certification language.

REQ-07-05-009: the future implementation shall include UI tests or equivalent review evidence for category availability, unit labels, warning/blocked states, status separation, and report/export handoff signals.
No external engineering code or standards text is introduced by this deliverable; controlling references are the OpenPipeStress governance and technical documents listed in _REFERENCES.md.

Any future rule-check wording, stress ratio threshold, allowable, code category, or formula must come from a user-supplied or lawfully imported private rule pack and must preserve provenance and redistribution status.
